column1: # Known refusals: our open gaps, each one an OPEN BUG with a todo behind it.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a refusal of something plain Metal does — which, by the owner's standing rule
# that what Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours — written down so the one case that holds
# it visible does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted
# difference lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade
# catalogue and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
# directions:
#   - a refusal that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that is NOT refused any more ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` row, with our error, with Metal's own words where its API validation refuses the call
# too, and counted in the suite's own `refused` number. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected, so replaying one case does not read every
# other row as fixed.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
# case
column4: the gap it is waiting on

column1: rate-map-zero-screen-width
column3: Err(Error::Invalid("invalid use of new_rasterization_rate_map: RateMap(ScreenSize { width: 0, height: 64 })"))
column4: The runtime refuses a rasterization-rate map of zero screen width, where plain Metal compiles one and answers queries over it (screen 0x64x1, physicalSizeForLayer:0 of 0x33x1, 24,624 parameter bytes). Metal's own API validation refuses the descriptor, but a validated stop is not Metal refusing the call, so this is ours to fix: metal2vulkan-runtime/src/rate_map.rs, `validate`, RateMapProblem::ScreenSize. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

column1: mesh-object-draws-partial-threadgroup-6-by-4
column3: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column4: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state, while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. metal2vulkan's mesh bind state, the partial-object-threadgroup path. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.
